name: Isolated Microspherophakia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnostic criteria for isolated microspherophakia

criteria.description: Presence of small, spherical crystalline lenses confirmed by slit-lamp examination or imaging
No clinical or genetic evidence of systemic syndromes associated with microspherophakia (e.g., Weill-Marchesani syndrome)
Ectopia lentis or lens subluxation observed clinically or via imaging
Elevated intraocular pressure or secondary glaucoma documented
Positive family history of isolated microspherophakia or autosomal recessive inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of small spherical lenses with absence of systemic features; lens dislocation and elevated intraocular pressure support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may help exclude syndromic causes; diagnosis is primarily clinical and ophthalmological.

pathognomonic.notes: Small, spherical lens shape confirmed by slit-lamp or imaging
Partial displacement of the lens from its normal position

common.notes: Elevated intraocular pressure due to pupillary block
Refractive error caused by altered lens shape
Reduced space between cornea and iris

occasional.notes: Shaking or trembling of the lens on eye movement
Damage to corneal endothelial cells secondary to lens abnormalities
Thinning or degeneration of the iris tissue
Pain episodes related to elevated intraocular pressure
searchTerms: eye pain that comes and goes

rare.notes: Separation of retina from underlying tissue
Swelling of the cornea due to fluid accumulation

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing spherical lens morphology
Ultrasound biomicroscopy confirming lens size and position
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrating shallow anterior chamber
genetic: Exclusion of mutations associated with syndromic microspherophakia (e.g., ADAMTS10, FBN1)
Possible autosomal recessive inheritance pattern in isolated cases
other: Visual field testing showing glaucomatous changes

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic features including short stature, brachydactyly, joint stiffness
Genetic mutations in ADAMTS10 or FBN1
Ectopia lentis but typically normal lens shape

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe ocular pain and vision loss indicating acute angle-closure glaucoma
Rapidly increasing intraocular pressure unresponsive to medical therapy
Signs of optic nerve damage or visual field loss
references: Kumar A, et al. Isolated microspherophakia: clinical features and management. Eye (Lond). 2019;33(2):234-241.
Weiss AH, et al. Microspherophakia and lens dislocation: clinical and genetic aspects. Surv Ophthalmol. 2018;63(3):345-357.
